reviews.text:
I came here on a referral from my regular veterinarian.
My dog ​​ate some hard cheese, which chipped a molar and exposed the pulp.
The treatment was accurate and speedy. Even though they were very busy, Dr. Toda, the nurses, and the reception staff were all very polite.
They were very gentle with dogs and gave me, the owner, accurate advice.
My dog ​​now lets me brush his teeth happily, just like before.
It really feels like a dog dentist's office.
The price isn't cheap, but they explain everything thoroughly.

They didn't really listen to my concerns or examine my dog ​​thoroughly, and they immediately recommended surgery, which I assume was a general opinion. I decided it wasn't the right fit for us.

I understand the need for a thorough examination under anesthesia, but based on my dog's history, even I, as the owner, didn't think surgery was necessary. I went back to the specialist vet we saw before moving, and they confirmed that surgery wasn't necessary; in fact, a little more effort with daily brushing would be sufficient.

I realized I'd been a bit lax with brushing, so I resumed diligent daily brushing, and the problem I was concerned about disappeared.

Even if extraction wasn't necessary, surgery carries the risk of unnecessary anesthesia and stress, so I decided it wasn't right for us and gave it a rating of 1.

I believe compatibility with the vet and intuition are important, so I'm sorry, but I don't think I'll be visiting that vet again.

However, the reception staff were friendly and chatted with me, which was nice.

My Chihuahua (1 kg) was treated at this clinic after being introduced by a friend whose dog breeder's kennel is the same as mine. Just before turning one year old, my dog's mouth was in poor condition due to retained deciduous teeth, so I specifically requested the head dentist. The doctor explained everything thoroughly, and after taking X-rays under general anesthesia, the unnecessary deciduous teeth were extracted. My concern was general anesthesia for such a small dog, but the doctor managed the anesthesia perfectly, and there were no problems. Some of the canine teeth remain impacted due to underdeveloped lower jaw, but since forcibly extracting them could risk damaging the jawbone, the optimal treatment was provided. The cost was as quoted (or even lower).

Later, trusting Dr. Toda's skill and sincere approach, I asked him to clean the teeth of my 12-year-old senior dog (Chihuahua, 3 kg). For dogs over 10 years old, a health check is required beforehand to determine if they can withstand general anesthesia. As a result, we discovered early-stage bladder cancer. When the ultrasound revealed that the cancer had spread, it came as a complete shock, and I was left completely bewildered. Thanks to Dr. Toda's help, we were able to have surgery at another hospital promptly. Currently, Dr. Toda is receiving the latest treatment with molecularly targeted drugs at the University of Tokyo's Faculty of Agriculture Veterinary Medical Center and is remarkably healthy. Other doctors were also surprised by Dr. Toda's imaging diagnosis in detecting the early-stage bladder cancer. I am truly grateful to Dr. Toda. When I visited to express my gratitude afterward, he treated me with sincerity, and I am so glad that we were able to receive care at this hospital.

Previously, we had regular anesthesia-free dental scaling, but it not only stresses the dog but also damages the enamel and doesn't remove bacteria from periodontal pockets. While surgery carries the risk of exposing my beloved dog to general anesthesia, Dr. Toda's anesthesia management was trustworthy. His ultrasound image interpretation, diagnosis, and surgical skills are also highly reliable. Although he is a primary care doctor rooted in the local community, I am so glad that we found such a doctor with god-level skills. Thank you very much.

The nurses are kind, and the doctor explains things in detail. It is on the smaller side, but the treatment rooms are not bad, and the automated payment system is nice. Parking is a bit inconvenient (there are two parking lots located 3-5 minutes walk from the hospital).

There might be some nice people, but generally, everyone's attitude is cold.

The waiting room is small, and the staff are always rushing around, so the animals can't relax.

Their technical skills might be good, but based on their attitude and how they treat the animals, I can't trust the entire hospital.

I wish they would treat each animal with more kindness and love, not just technical skill. All of them.

I don't understand why they're even running a veterinary hospital.

It was a completely unsuitable place for me.

I went to this clinic because they specialize in teeth. The doctor's diagnosis was excellent. I had been getting a health checkup every six months, but it was here that we found out my pet had kidney disease. I could tell them he had a lot of experience seeing many animals. He patiently explained things he didn't know using books. All the staff were kind and it was a really good hospital. I realized that you should definitely entrust dental care to a dental specialist.

One of my pets has senior kidney disease, so we decided against dental surgery. Another pet has respiratory problems, and we were told to go to a university hospital.

The staff told me that it would be difficult for my pet to recover from kidney disease, so it would be better to go back to our local vet.

The staff seemed like a surgical team and were very reliable.

It was tough afterward, but my pet's condition has improved considerably.

The doctor doesn't seem interested in pets that can't undergo dental surgery. That's the only downside.
